subtitle: Midterm Important Subjective Questions (Solved)
topics: The Novel and the Short Story

subjective.question: Write a short note on the life and poetry of Mir Taqi Mir.
subjective.answer: Mir Taqi Mir (1723-1810) is regarded as the 'Khuda-e-Sukhan' (God of poetry) of Urdu. He lived in Delhi during its decline and witnessed the invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali, so the pain of the ruined city fills his verse. His ghazal expresses deep sorrow, love and the instability of life in a simple yet heart-touching diction. Mir's influence on later poets, especially Nasir Kazmi, is profound, and his Diwan is a treasure of the Urdu ghazal.

subjective.question: Discuss the salient features of Mirza Ghalib's poetry.
subjective.answer: Ghalib's poetry is marked by depth of thought, philosophy and a unique, difficult style (Mushkil Pasandi) adopted under the influence of the Persian poet Bedil. His concept of love is full of 'ananiyat' (ego and self-respect): the lover preserves his dignity even before the beloved. Wit and playfulness (shokhi-o-zarafat) are part of his temperament, and his verses carry multiple layers of meaning. His poetry is usually divided into three periods, the third being the Persian period.

subjective.question: What is meant by Ghalib's 'Mushkil Pasandi'? Name the poet who influenced it.
subjective.answer: Mushkil Pasandi means Ghalib's preference for a complex, difficult and thought-laden style in which a single verse carries several meanings and demands deep reflection from the reader. Ghalib adopted this style under the influence of the famous Persian poet Mirza Abdul Qadir Bedil, whose intricate metaphors and philosophical depth Ghalib admired and imitated in his early poetry.

subjective.question: Why is Allama Iqbal called 'Musawwir-e-Pakistan'?
subjective.answer: Allama Muhammad Iqbal presented the concept of a separate homeland for the Muslims of the subcontinent in his Allahabad Address of 1930 and awakened the Muslims through his poetry. Because he painted the very picture (tasweer) of Pakistan in the minds of the Muslims before its creation, he is honoured with the title 'Musawwir-e-Pakistan' — the artist who envisioned Pakistan.

subjective.question: Discuss Akbar Allahabadi's method of reforming the nation through satire and humour.
subjective.answer: Akbar Allahabadi (1846-1921), known as 'Lisan-ul-Asr', took up the task of reforming the nation not through sermons but through satire and humour (tanz-o-zarafat). He targeted blind imitation of the West, hollow modernity, religious hypocrisy and social evils, presenting serious criticism in a light, witty style that made the reader laugh and think at the same time. His humorous verse remains a model of purposeful comic poetry in Urdu.

subjective.question: Write a short note on Altaf Hussain Hali's services to Urdu literature.
subjective.answer: Altaf Hussain Hali (1837-1914) was a poet, critic and biographer and a close associate of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. His 'Musaddas-e-Hali' (Mad-o-Jazar-e-Islam, 1879) awakened the Muslims by depicting their past glory and present decline. He founded modern criticism in Urdu through 'Muqaddama-e-Sher-o-Shairi' and wrote famous biographies such as 'Yadgar-e-Ghalib', 'Hayat-e-Saadi' and 'Hayat-e-Javed'. He is especially known for biography writing (sawanh nigari).

subjective.question: Write a short note on Hafeez Jalandhari's poetry.
subjective.answer: Hafeez Jalandhari (1900-1982), born in Jalandhar, is famous for his long poem 'Shahnama-e-Islam', which narrates Islamic history in verse in a simple, flowing style. He remained the editor of the magazine 'Makhzan' and wrote popular poems such as 'Chaman ki Sair'. He is also the author of Pakistan's national anthem. His poetry combines religious fervour, patriotism and musicality.

subjective.question: Discuss the distinguishing features of Majeed Amjad's poetry.
subjective.answer: Majeed Amjad (1914-1974) is a thoughtful modern poet whose verse is dominated by philosophy and reflection. A central aspect of his poetry is his 'tasawwur-e-waqt' (concept of time); he presents time as a flowing, changing reality. Poems like 'Tausi-e-Shahar' and 'Aik Kohistani Safar Ke Dauran' show his keen observation of nature and modern city life, expressed in a quiet, meditative tone quite different from his contemporaries.

subjective.question: Discuss the salient features of Faiz Ahmed Faiz's poetry.
subjective.answer: Faiz Ahmed Faiz (1911-1984) blended the classical ghazal tradition with progressive thought. His poetry joins love of the beloved with love of the homeland — he portrays the watan in the image of the beloved — and voices the suffering of the oppressed. An 'ananiyat' similar to Ghalib's is also found in him. His famous poem 'Dhaka Se Wapsi Par', written in ghazal form on the Fall of Dhaka, shows his deep pain at national tragedies. He died in 1984.

subjective.question: Why is Nasir Kazmi called a poet of nostalgia (Mazi Prasti)? Also mention Mir's influence on him.
subjective.answer: Nostalgia (mazi prasti) is the major quality of Nasir Kazmi's poetry: his ghazals repeatedly mourn the lost past — ruined cities, departed friends and vanished gatherings — in refrains such as 'kia huay' (what became of them?). Born in Ambala in 1925, he settled in Lahore and broadcast the programme 'Safina-e-Ghazal' from Radio Lahore. The influence of Mir Taqi Mir, along with Fani Badayuni and Firaq Gorakhpuri, is clearly visible in his diction and mood; the metaphor of the night (raat) recurs throughout his verse.

subjective.question: Discuss the style and features of Ghalib's letters.
subjective.answer: Ghalib's letters founded modern Urdu prose; they are called the first landmark (naqsh-e-awwal) of modern Urdu prose. Their most prominent feature is the elimination of formal etiquette: Ghalib dropped lengthy titles and salutations, used very brief forms of address, and wrote in a conversational, friendly tone, as if talking to the reader. His collections include 'Urdu-e-Mualla' (published in his lifetime), 'Oud-e-Hindi' and 'Makateeb-e-Ghalib' (compiled by Imtiaz Ali Arshi); Khaleeq Anjum later compiled 'Khutoot-e-Ghalib' in three volumes.

subjective.question: Write a note on the evolution of Urdu prose, mentioning the role of the Sufis and Fort William College.
subjective.answer: The Sufis (Sufiya-e-Kiram) played the first important role in the evolution of Urdu prose by using the people's language to preach and guide, producing early religious prose in the Deccan. A decisive step came with Fort William College (established 1800 in Calcutta), where, under Dr John Gilchrist, Indian scholars such as Mir Aman wrote and translated simple prose works like 'Bagh-o-Bahar'. The college is called the first standard milestone of Urdu prose, after which Ghalib's letters gave modern Urdu prose its first landmark.

subjective.question: Write a short note on the essays of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
subjective.answer: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (1817-1898) used the essay (mazmoon) as an instrument of reform. His essays, published largely in his journal 'Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq', deal with education, morality, religion and the social condition of the Muslims. His prose is clear, logical and purposeful, free of ornamental rhyming prose; he argued rationally against blind tradition and for modern education, laying the foundation of modern Urdu essay writing.

subjective.question: What is a Dastaan? Discuss 'Sab Ras' as an allegorical dastaan.
subjective.answer: A dastaan is a long, marvellous tale full of magic, adventure and supernatural events, narrated to entertain. Mulla Wajhi's 'Sab Ras' (1635), also called 'Qissa-e-Husn-o-Dil', is the first literary work of Urdu and an allegorical (tamseeli) dastaan: its characters — Husn (beauty), Dil (heart), Aqal (reason) and Ishq (love) — represent abstract qualities, and the story symbolises the inner struggle of man. It is a translation-adaptation of a Persian tale.

subjective.question: Write a note on Mir Aman and his 'Bagh-o-Bahar'.
subjective.answer: Mir Aman Dehlvi wrote 'Bagh-o-Bahar' at Fort William College, translating the Persian 'Qissa Chahar Darwesh' into simple, idiomatic Urdu. The book belongs to the dastaan genre, but its language is close to everyday speech. In it Mir Aman revived the culture of Delhi (Dehlvi tehzeeb) — its manners, idioms and daily life — making the book a living picture of old Delhi as well as a milestone of Urdu prose.

subjective.question: Write a note on Rajab Ali Baig Suroor and 'Fasana-e-Ajaaib'.
subjective.answer: Rajab Ali Baig Suroor wrote 'Fasana-e-Ajaaib' as a reaction to 'Bagh-o-Bahar', deliberately using ornate, rhymed and difficult prose to prove Urdu's literary capacity. The dastaan is a mirror of Lucknow's culture (Lucknowi tehzeeb) — its courtly life, fairs, manners and speech. Though its style is artificial compared with Mir Aman's simplicity, it holds a unique place in Urdu prose for its rich depiction of Lucknow civilisation.

subjective.topic: The Novel and the Short Story
subjective.question: Discuss Deputy Nazir Ahmad as a novelist, with reference to 'Mirat-ul-Uroos'.
subjective.answer: Deputy Nazir Ahmad (1830-1912) is the first novelist of Urdu. He wrote didactic, reformative novels for the education of women and society. His first novel 'Mirat-ul-Uroos' (1869) — 'the mirror of the bride' — was written for his daughters; its preface states his aim of reforming women's ideas and habits through an interesting story. His other novels include 'Banat-un-Nash' (reform of girls), 'Taubat-un-Nasuh' (social reform; main character Zahir Dar Baig), 'Ibn-ul-Waqt' and 'Ayami' (the plight of widows).

subjective.topic: The Novel and the Short Story
subjective.question: Write the themes of the novels 'Taubat-un-Nasuh', 'Banat-un-Nash' and 'Ayami'.
subjective.answer: 'Taubat-un-Nasuh' by Deputy Nazir Ahmad is a novel of social and moral reform in which the reformed life of Nasuh and the character of Zahir Dar Baig stand out. 'Banat-un-Nash', also by Nazir Ahmad, concerns the reform and proper upbringing of girls. 'Ayami', another of his novels, depicts the miserable plight of widows in society and pleads for sympathy and justice towards them.

subjective.topic: The Novel and the Short Story
subjective.question: What are the elements (ajza-e-tarkeebi) of a novel? Also define a 'straight plot'.
subjective.answer: The main elements of a novel are: plot, characterisation (kirdar nigari), setting of time and place (mahol, zaman-o-makan), dialogue, and depiction of scenes (manzar nigari). A straight plot (mustaqeem plot) is one in which the story begins at a particular point and proceeds in a straight line to its logical end, without sub-plots or complications.

subjective.topic: The Novel and the Short Story
subjective.question: Write a short note on Prem Chand as a short-story writer.
subjective.answer: Munshi Prem Chand (1880-1936), whose real name was Dhanpat Rai, is the greatest short-story writer and novelist of Urdu and Hindi. His stories such as 'Kafan' and 'Zaad-e-Raah' portray the life of peasants, poverty, injustice and the decay of the feudal order with deep realism and sympathy. His characters are drawn from ordinary life, and his simple, powerful language made the Urdu afsana a serious art form.

subjective.topic: The Novel and the Short Story
subjective.question: Write a note on Sajjad Haider Yildirim as a pioneer of the Urdu short story.
subjective.answer: Sajjad Haider Yildirim (1880-1943) is regarded as the first short-story writer (afsana nigar) of Urdu. His collection of stories was published under the name 'Khayalistan'. Influenced by Turkish and Western literature, he introduced romance, individual freedom and criticism of outdated customs into Urdu fiction; his famous stories include 'Mujhe Mere Doston Se Bachao' and 'Jari Charhe Ki Kahani'.

subjective.question: What is Sawaneh Umri (biography)? Give its definition and features.
subjective.answer: The word 'sawaneh' is Arabic. Sawaneh Umri is that form of history which relates not to nations and groups but to individuals: it presents a person's complete journey of life from the cradle to the grave — his character, habits, psychology and the ups and downs of his life — in an interesting literary style, so that the whole personality stands before the reader. Unlike the old tradition of merely praising achievements, the modern biographer presents verified facts critically and truthfully.

subjective.question: Write a note on Shibli Nomani as a biographer (sawanh nigar).
subjective.answer: Allama Shibli Nomani (1857-1914) raised Urdu biography to the level of research and criticism. His biographies are all of the heroes of Islamic history: 'Al-Farooq' (on Hazrat Umar), 'Al-Mamoon', 'Al-Ghazali', 'Sawaneh Maulana Rum' and his masterpiece 'Seerat-un-Nabi (PBUH)'. He combined historical research, critical judgement and a flowing literary style, and founded the Dar-ul-Musannifeen at Azamgarh to promote such scholarship.

subjective.question: Differentiate between fictional (afsanvi) and non-fictional (ghair afsanvi) literature.
subjective.answer: Fictional literature (afsanvi adab) is the literature of imagination and story; it includes the dastaan, the novel, the short story (afsana) and drama. Non-fictional literature (ghair afsanvi adab) is based on fact and exposition; it includes essay writing (mazmoon nigari), insha-pardazi, report-writing, letter-writing, biography and criticism, in which there is no element of invented story.

subjective.question: Define the following terms of poetry: Matla, Maqta, Radeef and Qafia.
subjective.answer: Matla is the first couplet of a ghazal, in which both lines carry the same qafia and radeef. Maqta is the last couplet of a ghazal, in which the poet usually uses his pen-name (takhallus). Radeef is the word or phrase repeated at the end of each couplet after the rhyme. Qafia is the rhyming word that comes just before the radeef and changes its form in every couplet while keeping the same sound pattern.

subjective.question: Define Tashbih, Istiara and Talmih with brief explanations.
subjective.answer: Tashbih (simile) is comparing one thing with another on the basis of a shared quality, e.g. a face like the moon. Istiara (metaphor) is attributing the qualities of one thing to another and using a word in a sense other than its literal one, e.g. calling a brave man a lion. Talmih (allusion) is the brief reference to a Quranic verse, a Hadith or a historical event in such a way that the verse or sentence cannot be fully understood without knowing that reference.

subjective.question: What is Tamseel Nigari (allegory)? Give an example from Urdu literature.
subjective.answer: Tamseel Nigari is the art of presenting abstract ideas, non-standard actions and traits in the form of characters, so that an idea becomes a living person in the story. The best early example in Urdu is Mulla Wajhi's 'Sab Ras', in which Husn, Dil, Aqal and Ishq appear as characters and their conflict represents the inner moral struggle of man.

subjective.question: What is the basic element of romantic poetry (Romani Shayari)? Discuss briefly.
subjective.answer: The basic element of romantic poetry is nature (fitrat). Romantic poets turn away from rigid rules and social restraints towards emotion, imagination, individual freedom and the beauty of nature. In Urdu, Akhtar Shirani is the most prominent name in romantic poetry; his verse is dominated by love, beauty and the colours of nature, expressed in a musical and emotional style.
